accuracy.evidence: Every pair used is a standard English antonym pair (hot/cold, wet/dry, up/down, happy/sad, open/closed, awake/asleep, on/off, day/night, loud/quiet, fast/slow, big/little), every 'same' pair is a synonym pair (big/large, happy/glad, fast/quick), and cat, chair, red and dog are words with no conventional antonym. The lesson does not claim every word has an opposite or that opposites are only sizes. DfE Development Matters 2021 Reception vocabulary and the EYFS ELG Speaking are cited for the age; Murphy and Jones 2008 for antonym pairs being frequent in child and child-directed speech and often said together. Numeric items are simple counts (pairs, cups, children) with ranges kept within 10.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented young-child slips: choosing a thematically associated word instead of the antonym (fire for hot, rain for wet, sky for up, smile for happy, key for open; prediction 1; challenge tag goes), treating synonyms as opposites (big/large, happy/glad, fast/quick; prediction 2; tag same), over-extending opposites to words that have none (cat/dog; prediction 3; tag every), and swapping the wrong word in a sentence (tapping The, door, is; tag wrongword).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagopposite is built on this topic's own mechanism: a picture word with its opposite and an associated word as choices, a sentence whose one describing word flips and changes the picture (door opens and closes, baby wakes and sleeps, light goes on and off, towel wet and dry), a pair sort into opposites versus same meaning, a has-an-opposite decision, and a find-the-pairs grid. It is not the un- prefix builder of flagunpre or the size comparison of the measures labs. Gate: under 30% shingle overlap with every other flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child meets the idea through pictures: the thermometer goes from high red to low blue, the door picture changes when the word changes, so 'swap the word and it means the other thing' is seen. Sorting pairs then separates opposite from same, and the no-opposite step shows the limit of the idea. Each done message confirms in one short line; feedback names the slip ('Fire goes with hot, but it is not the other end').

predictions.evidence: Three predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab then disproves: 'fire' as the opposite of hot (the match step rejects associated words), 'big and large are opposites' (the sort step puts them in Mean the same), and 'dog is the opposite of cat' (the no-opposite step). Each step's done message reveals the locked-in prediction.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven challenge questions, each wrong option tagged to its own slip with its own message: goes (ice and snow for cold, sky for up, sun and morning for day, smile for happy), same (high, glad, 'Yes' for big/large), every (cat or puppy for dog) and wrongword (swapping bag or big instead of full). In-step feedback also names the word: '"The" has no opposite', 'A door has no opposite. Swap the word that tells what it is like'.

readability.evidence: Family lesson for ages 4 to 5: kid text in very short sentences of common words ('Hot and cold. Up and down.'), within the learn/readability.py limit; adult text within its limit. Every canvas card has a picture plus one word at 18 to 28 px, so a child who cannot read yet can do every step with a grown-up reading the heading aloud.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passes (no filler phrases, under 12% six-word overlap with any other lesson). Each kid paragraph teaches one point (what an opposite is, swapping flips the meaning, goes-with and same are not opposites, some words have none); the adult paragraphs give the curriculum link, why pairs are learned together, named mistakes and a lab summary.

mobile.evidence: Checked on iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark: picture cards are about 110 by 100 px, the sentence tiles fill the width at 70 px high, the two sort boxes and the Has an opposite / No opposite cards span half the width each, and the pairs grid is 2 columns of 3 on a phone. The young class gives large buttons under the canvas; nothing is clipped.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button: one per choice labelled 'The opposite of hot is cold', one per sentence word labelled with the whole sentence, Next, Opposites and Mean the same labelled with the pair, Has an opposite and No opposite labelled with the word, and one per pair card. say() updates the canvas aria-label and the polite live region after every action; the walk gate's axe run is clean (WCAG 2.1 AA) in both themes on desktop and iPhone.
